title: Section 95 — Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence

content.overview: BNS s. 95 — Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
New. Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence. The adult who uses a child as an instrument is punished; the child is the victim of this section.
In student language: BNS s. 95 is the rule on “Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence”. The section provides that whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 95 exists so that “Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
95. Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself

Punishment / legal consequence
Up to 10 years, and not less than 3 years, + fine; death of child: 7-to-life.

Explanations
Explanation.—Hiring, employing, engaging or using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography is covered within the meaning of this section

learningObjectives: Master the brand-new BNS substantive offence criminalizing the recruitment, hiring, or engagement of children in crime.
Analyze the dual sentencing structure: independent imprisonment of 3 to 10 years plus fine, along with co-extensive punishment as if the adult committed the substantive offence.
Understand the statutory Explanation expressly including child sexual exploitation and child pornography under s. 95.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 95 establishes a new substantive offence punishing whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed, shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself. The Explanation covers hiring, employing, engaging or using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Adult criminal exploitation of minors is subjected to primary and vicarious statutory liability to dismantle criminal enterprises utilizing children as shields from standard penal consequences.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 95 (brand-new substantive provision in BNS 2023).
Actus reus: Hiring, employing, or engaging any child (person under eighteen years) to commit an offence.
Independent penalty: Imprisonment not less than three years, extending up to ten years, and fine.
Cumulative penalty: If the offence is actually committed, the person is also punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if committed by himself.
Explanation: Expressly includes hiring, employing, engaging, or using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography within the section.
essentialIngredients: The person engaged or hired is a child (under eighteen years of age).
The accused hired, employed, or engaged the child.
The engagement was for the purpose of committing an offence (including sexual exploitation or pornography under the Explanation).
If the offence is committed, joint vicarious liability attaches co-extensively to the adult.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 95 is one of the most significant structural innovations introduced in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Historically, organized crime syndicates, drug cartels, and traffickers exploited the juvenile justice system by deploying minors to execute theft, transport contraband, or engage in violent crimes, knowing that children are protected from adult penal sentences. Section 95 decisively reverses this dynamic by targeting the adult mastermind. The provision creates an independent standalone crime punishable with a minimum of three years and up to ten years imprisonment for merely hiring or engaging the child. Furthermore, if the contemplated offence is actually carried out, the adult is punished with the full penalty prescribed for that completed offence as if they committed it with their own hands. The Explanation explicitly expands the scope to cover child sexual exploitation and pornography.
examples: Teaching example (Using minors for drug trafficking): An adult drug dealer hires two fourteen-year-old boys to transport commercial quantities of narcotics across city checkpoints. Even before the transport occurs, the dealer is guilty under s. 95. Once they deliver the drugs, the dealer is also punished with the full penalty under the narcotics laws as if he transported them himself.

Teaching example (Child exploitation under Explanation): An accused engages a seventeen-year-old minor to produce explicit digital media for an online platform. Under the Explanation to s. 95, this constitutes using a child for sexual exploitation/pornography, attracting severe liability under s. 95 alongside POCSO Act provisions.
distinctions: Section 95 vs General Abetment (s. 45): Abetment requires proving traditional instigation, conspiracy, or aid; Section 95 creates a distinct, strict substantive offence with mandatory minimum 3-year imprisonment specifically for hiring/employing a child.

Section 95 vs Juvenile Justice Act s. 75/78: Section 95 is a general penal code felony with direct vicarious punishment for the underlying crime, whereas JJ Act provisions focus on child welfare and cruelty infractions.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an adult gang leader who hired a 13-year-old child to carry out an armed robbery at a jewelry store can be prosecuted under s. 95 when the robbery was successfully executed by the child.

Rule: Under BNS s. 95, hiring a child to commit an offence is punishable with 3 to 10 years imprisonment, and if the offence is committed, with the punishment for that offence as if committed by the adult himself.
Application: The gang leader hired the minor and the robbery was committed.
Conclusion: The leader is guilty under s. 95 and faces robbery penalties co-extensively.

State the dual penalty: minimum 3 to 10 years for hiring, plus full punishment for the offence itself if committed.
Highlight the Explanation covering sexual exploitation and pornography.
